subproblem.title: Choice of a common good level for countably many a.e. properties, a summable family of slice masses and countably many measures
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and a < b real numbers. Let g_i : ℝ → [0, ∞] (i ∈ ℕ) be a.e.-measurable for Lebesgue measure restricted to (a, b), with Σ_i ∫_{(a,b)} g_i dt < ∞. Let μ_i (i ∈ ℕ) be measures on ℝ^P and h : ℝ^P → ℝ a measurable function with μ_i({a < h < b}) < ∞ for every i. Let good_i (i ∈ ℕ) be predicates on ℝ, each holding for L¹-a.e. t. Then there is t ∈ (a, b) such that good_i(t) holds for every i, Σ_i g_i(t) < ∞, and μ_i({h = t}) = 0 for every i.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (g : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ≥0∞) (μ : ℕ → Measure (Euclid P)) (h : Euclid P → ℝ) (good : ℕ → ℝ → Prop) (a b : ℝ), a < b → Measurable h → (∀ i, AEMeasurable (g i) (volume.restrict (Ioo a b))) → (∑' i, ∫⁻ t in Ioo a b, g i t) ≠ ∞ → (∀ i, μ i {x | a < h x ∧ h x < b} ≠ ∞) → (∀ i, ∀ᵐ t, good i t) → ∃ t ∈ Ioo a b, (∀ i, good i t) ∧ (∑' i, g i t) ≠ ∞ ∧ ∀ i, μ i {x | h x = t} = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof: "Choose α ∈ (0, 1) outside the union of the following null sets: the levels where for some i the slice is not IM or the slice identity fails (countably many null sets); the levels with Σ_i M(P_i(α)) = ∞; and the levels with μ_{S_{φ₁(i)}}(Σ_α) > 0 for some i (for each i these are countably many, because the Σ_α are pairwise disjoint subsets of … finite μ-measure)". Here the levels are t ∈ (a, b), the level sets are {h = t}, and the predicates good_i are abstract. λ denotes Lebesgue measure on ℝ.

1. (Failures of the predicates.) For each i, N_i := {t : ¬good_i(t)} is λ-null by hypothesis. So N := ⋃_i N_i is λ-null, as a countable union (Mathlib ae_all_iff).

2. (Summability.) Let λ_ab := λ⌞(a, b). Each g_i is λ_ab-a.e. measurable, so ∫_{(a,b)} Σ_i g_i dλ = Σ_i ∫_{(a,b)} g_i dλ < ∞ (lintegral_tsum), and Σ_i g_i is λ_ab-a.e. measurable. A non-negative a.e.-measurable function with finite integral is finite a.e. (ae_lt_top'). So N' := {t ∈ (a, b) : Σ_i g_i(t) = ∞} is λ-null.

3. (Atoms of the level sets.) Fix i and put ν_i := μ_i⌞{a < h < b}, a finite measure by hypothesis and hence s-finite.
 (a) Since h is measurable, the sets {h = t} are disjoint and measurable, and at most countably many of them have positive ν_i-measure. So C_i := {t : ν_i({h = t}) > 0} is countable (Mathlib Measure.countable_meas_level_set_pos).
 (b) For t ∈ (a, b), {h = t} ⊆ {a < h < b}, so μ_i({h = t}) = ν_i({h = t}). Hence μ_i({h = t}) = 0 for t ∈ (a, b) ∖ C_i.
 (c) C := ⋃_i C_i is countable, hence λ-null.

4. (Choice.) λ((a, b)) = b − a > 0, while N ∪ N' ∪ C is λ-null. So there is t ∈ (a, b) ∖ (N ∪ N' ∪ C). For this t: good_i(t) for all i (t ∉ N), Σ_i g_i(t) < ∞ (t ∉ N'), and μ_i({h = t}) = 0 for all i (t ∉ C). ∎
proof_key_steps: The failures of the predicates form a countable union of null sets.
Σ_i g_i has finite integral over (a, b), hence is finite a.e.
For each i, at most countably many level sets {h = t} carry μ_i-mass, because μ_i⌞{a < h < b} is finite.
(a, b) has positive measure, so some t avoids all exceptional sets.

audit.reason: Tonelli gives pointwise summability almost everywhere. Restricting each arbitrary measure to the finite-measure band justifies countability of charged levels. A positive-length interval contains a point avoiding all exceptional sets.

subproblem.title: Flat decomposition of weakly convergent integer multiplicity currents in ℝ^P (Simon 6.7.1–7.2, 'only if' part)
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ with n := m + 1 < P. Let T_j (j ∈ ℕ) and T be integer multiplicity currents in 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n with IsIntegerMultiplicity) such that sup_j (M_W(T_j) + M_W(∂T_j)) < ∞ for every bounded open W ⊆ ℝ^P, and T_j ⇀ T in ℝ^P (WeaklyConvergesOn: T_j(ω) → T(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P)). Then for every bounded open W ⊆ ℝ^P there are integer multiplicity currents R_j ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^P) and S_j ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (j ∈ ℕ) with T − T_j − S_j = ∂R_j for every j (Simon: T − T_j = ∂R_j + S_j) and M_W(R_j) + M_W(S_j) → 0. Here M_W is the SimonGMT mass massOn W (Euclidean coefficient norm).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (Ts : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)), m + 1 < P → (∀ j, IsIntegerMultiplicity (Ts j)) → IsIntegerMultiplicity T → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → Bornology.IsBounded W → ⨆ j, ((Ts j).massOn W + (Ts j).boundary.massOn W) < ∞) → WeaklyConvergesOn Ts T → ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → Bornology.IsBounded W → ∃ (R : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 2)) (S : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)), (∀ j, IsIntegerMultiplicity (R j) ∧ IsIntegerMultiplicity (S j) ∧ T - Ts j - S j = (R j).boundary) ∧ Tendsto (fun j => (R j).massOn W + (S j).massOn W) atTop (𝓝 0)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Definition 7.1 and the proof of the "only if" part of Theorem 7.2 (chapter-06.txt lines 2004–2120, printed pp. 170–172). Here U = ℝ^P, so "W ⊂⊂ U" means "W bounded", and the ambient dimension is n + ℓ = P with ℓ = P − n ≥ 1, the range n, ℓ ∈ {1, 2, …} of Simon §5. This is the result cited as (C1) in step 4 of the parent proof. The printed proof is copied. The details it leaves to the reader are written out in steps 3, 6 and 7: the localisation to a ball, the identification of the limit after localisation, and the passage from d_W(T_j, T) → 0 to explicit decompositions. In steps 4–6 the error currents S only need small mass; they need not be integer multiplicity. Integer multiplicity of the final error current is recovered in step 7 by applying boundary rectifiability to the (n+1)-current R^{(q)}. So every citation stays inside Simon's range (dimensions ≥ 1, codimension ℓ ≥ 1), also when m = 0.

Cited results of the source text, each used in its stated range:
(D) Simon 6.5.3, Deformation Theorem, scaled version (lines 1462–1480), for n-currents in ℝ^{n+ℓ}, n, ℓ ≥ 1. Let T ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with M(T) + M(∂T) < ∞ and let σ > 0. Then T − P = ∂R + S, where:
 • P = Σ_F β_F[[F]], the sum over the n-faces F of the cubical grid of side σ;
 • M(P) ≤ cM(T), M(R) ≤ cσM(T) and M(S) ≤ cσM(∂T), with c = c(n, ℓ);
 • spt P ∪ spt R ⊆ {x : dist(x, spt T) < 2√P σ} and spt S ⊆ {x : dist(x, spt ∂T) < 2√P σ}.
 If T is integer multiplicity, then P and R are integer multiplicity (β_F ∈ ℤ). Only these properties are used; S is just a current.
(BR) Simon 6.6.3, Boundary Rectifiability Theorem (lines 1993–1996). If T ∈ 𝒟_k(U) is integer multiplicity and M_V(∂T) < ∞ for all V ⊂⊂ U, then ∂T is integer multiplicity. It is used only for k = n + 1 ≥ 2.
(SL) Simon 6.4.6–4.10 (lines 1305–1385). Suppose M_V(T) + M_V(∂T) < ∞ for all V ⊂⊂ U and f is Lipschitz, and set ⟨T, f, t−⟩ := ∂(T⌞{f < t}) − (∂T)⌞{f < t}. Here T⌞E is the restriction of T to the Borel set E, defined through the measure representation of T (2.7).
 • (4.8) ⟨T, f, t−⟩ vanishes on every form whose support is disjoint from f⁻¹(t).
 • (4.9) For bounded open W: M_W(⟨T, f, t−⟩) ≤ ess sup_W|Df|·liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹ M_W(T⌞{t − h < f < t}).
 • The lower Dini derivative D(t) := liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹ μ_T(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}) of the nondecreasing function t ↦ μ_T(W ∩ {f < t}) is measurable, with ∫_a^b D dt ≤ μ_T(W ∩ {a < f < b}). This is Lebesgue's theorem for monotone functions, which is how 4.10 is derived.
(ML) Elementary mass localisation. Let X be a current that vanishes on every form whose support is disjoint from a compact set C, and let V ⊇ C be open. Then M(X) ≤ M_V(X). Proof: choose χ ∈ C_c^∞(V) with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1 and χ = 1 on a neighbourhood of C. For every admissible ω, tsupport((1 − χ)ω) is disjoint from C and χω is admissible for M_V, so X(ω) = X(χω) + X((1 − χ)ω) = X(χω) ≤ M_V(X).
(CO) Simon 6.3.13 (lines 905–960). Integer multiplicity currents are complete for the seminorms M_V, V ⊂⊂ U. In particular, an M-absolutely convergent series of integer multiplicity currents with supports in a fixed compact set converges in mass to an integer multiplicity current.
(R) Integer combinations of integer multiplicity currents are integer multiplicity (Simon 6.3.2(1); sibling im_calculus (c)). The restriction (M ∩ E, θ, ξ) of a representation to a Borel set E represents an integer multiplicity current (sibling im_calculus (b)).
(MM) M_V(A) = μ_A(V) for integer multiplicity A and open V (sibling mass_eq_measure), and μ_A is finite on compact sets.
(LSC) Lower semicontinuity of mass under weak convergence (Simon 6.2.14; SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf).

Throughout, n := m + 1, ℓ := P − n ≥ 1, B_r := ball(0, r), and "IM" means integer multiplicity. For currents A, B in one domain and any V: M_V(0 − A) = M_V(A), since ω ↦ −ω preserves admissible forms, and M_V(A ± B) ≤ M_V(A) + M_V(B).

1. (The class I and the pseudometrics.) Let I be the set of IM currents A ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with M_V(∂A) < ∞ for every bounded open V.
 (a) Each T_j ∈ I by hypothesis.
 (b) T ∈ I: ∂T_j ⇀ ∂T, because ∂T_j(ω) = T_j(dω) → T(dω). So by (LSC), M_V(∂T) ≤ liminf_j M_V(∂T_j) ≤ sup_j (M_V(T_j) + M_V(∂T_j)) < ∞.
 (c) For A₁, A₂ ∈ I and bounded open V put (Simon 7.1) d_V(A₁, A₂) := inf{M_V(S) + M_V(R) : A₁ − A₂ = ∂R + S, with R ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^P) and S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) IM}. The set is nonempty: R = 0 and S = A₁ − A₂, which is IM by (R).

2. (Reduction.) Fix a bounded open W. It suffices to show d_W(T_j, T) → 0.
 (a) Suppose d_W(T_j, T) → 0. For each j choose IM R'_j, S'_j with T_j − T = ∂R'_j + S'_j and M_W(R'_j) + M_W(S'_j) ≤ d_W(T_j, T) + 2^{−j}. Put R_j := 0 − R'_j and S_j := 0 − S'_j, which are IM by (R).
 (b) Then T − T_j − S_j = −(T_j − T) + S'_j = −∂R'_j = ∂R_j, and M_W(R_j) + M_W(S_j) = M_W(R'_j) + M_W(S'_j) → 0.
 (c) Since (d_W(T_j, T))_j is a sequence in [0, ∞], it tends to 0 as soon as every subsequence has a further subsequence along which it tends to 0. This is Simon's last paragraph: "since we can thus extract a subsequence converging relative to d_W̃ from any given subsequence …". So fix an arbitrary subsequence; we keep calling it (T_j) and pass to further subsequences below.

3. (Localisation.) Simon: "by 4.5(1),(2) and an argument as in 6.7(2) of Ch. 2 we can find a subsequence … with sup_j' M(∂(T_j'⌞W_i)) < ∞ … thus we can assume … spt T_j ⊆ W̄".
 (a) Choose r₀ ≥ 1 with W ⊆ B_{r₀} and let f(x) := |x|, a 1-Lipschitz function. Put V := B_{r₀+2} and Λ := sup_j (M_V(T_j) + M_V(∂T_j)) < ∞.
 (b) Fix j and t ∈ (r₀, r₀ + 1). By 4.8 the slice ⟨T_j, f, t−⟩ vanishes on forms whose support misses the compact set f⁻¹(t) = ∂B_t ⊆ V, so M(⟨T_j, f, t−⟩) ≤ M_V(⟨T_j, f, t−⟩) by (ML). By 4.9 with W = V and |Df| ≤ 1, this is at most liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹ M_V(T_j⌞{t − h < f < t}). Since {t − h < f < t} ⊆ V for 0 < h < t, the restriction T_j⌞{t − h < f < t} is IM by (R) with weight μ_{T_j}⌞{t − h < f < t}, and by (MM) its mass in V is μ_{T_j}({t − h < f < t}). Hence M(⟨T_j, f, t−⟩) ≤ D_j(t) := liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹ μ_{T_j}(V ∩ {t − h < f < t}). D_j is measurable, and ∫_{r₀}^{r₀+1} D_j dt ≤ μ_{T_j}(V) = M_V(T_j) ≤ Λ by (MM).
 (c) By Fatou's lemma, ∫_{r₀}^{r₀+1} liminf_j D_j dt ≤ Λ. So there is t₀ ∈ (r₀, r₀ + 1) with liminf_j D_j(t₀) < ∞. Pass to a subsequence along which Λ' := sup_j M(⟨T_j, f, t₀−⟩) < ∞.
 (d) Put W₁ := B_{t₀} and T'_j := T_j⌞W₁. T'_j is IM by (R), being represented by (M_j ∩ W₁, θ_j, ξ_j). Moreover spt T'_j ⊆ closure(W₁) and ∂T'_j = (∂T_j)⌞W₁ + ⟨T_j, f, t₀−⟩. By (MM) with V = ℝ^P, M(T'_j) = μ_{T_j}(W₁) ≤ M_V(T_j). Also M((∂T_j)⌞W₁) ≤ μ_{∂T_j}(W₁) ≤ M_V(∂T_j), where μ_{∂T_j} is the Radon measure representing ∂T_j (2.7). Hence M(T'_j) + M(∂T'_j) ≤ Λ + Λ' =: M₀ for all j.
 (e) T'_j(ω) = T_j(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ W₁.
 (f) closure(W) ⊆ closedBall(0, r₀) ⊆ W₁.
 Let 𝒞 be the set of IM A ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with spt A ⊆ closure(W₁) and M(A) + M(∂A) ≤ M₀. All T'_j lie in 𝒞.

4. (Total boundedness; Simon (1)–(3).) Let W̃ := B_{t₀+1}.
 Claim: for every ε > 0 there are finitely many IM currents P₁, …, P_N ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) such that every A ∈ 𝒞 admits some k ≤ N, an IM R ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^P) and a current S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with A − P_k = ∂R + S, spt R ∪ spt S ⊆ W̃ and M(R) + M(S) < ε.
 (a) Choose σ ∈ (0, 1) with 2√P σ < 1 and cσM₀ < ε.
 (b) Let A ∈ 𝒞. A is IM with M(A) + M(∂A) ≤ M₀ < ∞, so (D) gives IM P, R and a current S with A − P = ∂R + S and M(R) + M(S) ≤ cσ(M(A) + M(∂A)) < ε. The supports of P, R and S lie within 2√P σ of spt A ∪ spt ∂A ⊆ closure(W₁), hence in W̃.
 (c) P = Σ_F β_F[[F]] with β_F ∈ ℤ and M(P) = Σ_F |β_F|σⁿ ≤ cM₀. Since spt P ⊆ W̃, only the finitely many n-faces F of the σ-grid meeting the bounded set W̃ occur, and |β_F| ≤ cM₀σ^{−n}.
 (d) So P belongs to a finite set {P₁, …, P_N} that depends only on ε, M₀, W₁, n and ℓ.

5. (A Cauchy subsequence; Simon (5).)
 (a) Apply step 4 with ε = 2^{−r−2} for r = 1, 2, …. subproblem.title: Subadditivity of the weights of integer multiplicity currents: μ_{X + cY} ≤ μ_X + μ_Y for |c| ≤ 1
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, and X, Y, Z ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with integer multiplicity representations R_X, R_Y, R_Z in U (IMRep U n). Let c ∈ ℝ with |c| ≤ 1, and suppose Z(ω) = X(ω) + c·Y(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Then the weights satisfy μ_Z ≤ μ_X + μ_Y as measures on ℝ^P, where μ_• := R_•.measure = θ_•Hⁿ⌞M_•. That is, μ_Z(E) ≤ μ_X(E) + μ_Y(E) for every E ⊆ ℝ^P.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (X Y Z : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (RX RY RZ : IMRep U n) (c : ℝ), IsOpen U → |c| ≤ 1 → RX.Represents X → RY.Represents Y → RZ.Represents Z → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Z ω = X ω + c * Y ω) → RZ.measure ≤ RX.measure + RY.measure
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 0, fact (F4) of the parent proof: "μ_{A±B}(E) ≤ μ_A(E) + μ_B(E) for every Borel E: for open E because M_E(A ± B) ≤ M_E(A) + M_E(B) (each admissible ω gives (A ± B)(ω) ≤ M_E(A) + M_E(B), as ±ω is admissible), and for Borel E by outer regularity of these locally finite Borel measures". Here it is stated for Z = X + cY with |c| ≤ 1; c = ±1 gives A ± B.

Notation. μ_X := R_X.measure = θ_XHⁿ⌞M_X, and similarly for Y and Z. M_V = massOn V is the supremum of ofReal T(ω) over ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ V and |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y (Euclidean coefficient norm).

1. (Mass triangle on open sets.) Let V ⊆ ℝ^P be open and ω admissible for M_V. Then −ω is admissible too, since tsupport(−ω) = tsupport ω and |−α| = |α|. So X(ω) ≤ M_V(X) and |Y(ω)| = max(Y(ω), Y(−ω)) ≤ M_V(Y), in [0, ∞] (SimonGMT le_massOn). Hence Z(ω) = X(ω) + cY(ω) ≤ M_V(X) + |c||Y(ω)| ≤ M_V(X) + M_V(Y), so ofReal Z(ω) ≤ M_V(X) + M_V(Y). Taking the supremum, M_V(Z) ≤ M_V(X) + M_V(Y). (This step is the comparator-accepted declaration lcmp_massOn_le_add_of_eval_eq with G := V.)

2. (Open subsets of U.) For open V ⊆ U the sibling mass_eq_measure gives M_V(•) = μ_•(V) for • ∈ {X, Y, Z}. With step 1, μ_Z(V) ≤ μ_X(V) + μ_Y(V).

3. (Concentration on U.) The carriers lie in U, so μ_•(E) = μ_•(E ∩ U) for every Borel E.

4. (Exhaustion and local finiteness.) For k ≥ 1 let
 K_k := {x ∈ U : |x| ≤ k, dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ U) ≥ 1/k} (K_k := closedBall(0, k) if U = ℝ^P),
 V_k := {x : |x| < k + 1, dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ U) > 1/(k + 1)} (V_k := B_{k+1}(0) if U = ℝ^P).
 Then K_k is compact, K_k ⊆ V_k ⊆ K_{k+1} ⊆ U, V_k is open and ⋃_k K_k = U. Since closure(V_k) ⊆ K_{k+1} is a compact subset of U, μ_•(V_k) ≤ μ_•(K_{k+1}) < ∞ (IMRep field locallyIntegrable_mult).

5. (Borel subsets of K_k.) Let E ⊆ K_k be Borel and δ > 0.
 (a) λ := (μ_X + μ_Y + μ_Z)⌞V_k is a finite Borel measure on the metric space ℝ^P, hence outer regular. So there is an open O ⊇ E with λ(O) ≤ λ(E) + δ.
 (b) Put O' := O ∩ V_k, an open set with E ⊆ O' ⊆ U. Then μ_•(O' ∖ E) ≤ λ(O ∖ E) = λ(O) − λ(E) ≤ δ for each •.
 (c) By step 2, μ_Z(E) ≤ μ_Z(O') ≤ μ_X(O') + μ_Y(O') ≤ μ_X(E) + μ_Y(E) + 2δ. Letting δ ↓ 0, μ_Z(E) ≤ μ_X(E) + μ_Y(E).

6. (All Borel sets.) For Borel E, the sets E ∩ K_k increase to E ∩ U. By step 5 and continuity from below, μ_Z(E ∩ U) ≤ μ_X(E ∩ U) + μ_Y(E ∩ U), i.e. μ_Z(E) ≤ μ_X(E) + μ_Y(E) by step 3. An inequality between measures may be checked on measurable sets (Measure.le_iff), so μ_Z ≤ μ_X + μ_Y. ∎
proof_key_steps: M_V(X + cY) ≤ M_V(X) + M_V(Y) for open V, since ±ω are both admissible and |c| ≤ 1. With mass_eq_measure this is μ_Z(V) ≤ μ_X(V) + μ_Y(V) for open V ⊆ U.
All three weights live on U and are finite on compact subsets of U.
Outer regularity of the finite measure (μ_X + μ_Y + μ_Z)⌞V_k extends the inequality to Borel subsets of K_k.
Exhaust U by compact sets and use continuity from below.

subproblem.title: A map fixing the support of an integer multiplicity current fixes its approximate tangent planes and orientation almost everywhere
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U, O ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity representation of T in U (IMRep U n with R.Represents T). Let f : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be differentiable at every point of O (DifferentiableOn ℝ f O) with f(y) = y for every y ∈ spt T ∩ O. Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ O (Hⁿ = μHE[n]): f(x) = x, and ⟨α ∘ ΛⁿDf(x), ξ(x)⟩ = ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ for every n-covector α. In Lean the last identity reads R.orient x (α.compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) = R.orient x α.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U O : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n) (f : Euclid P → Euclid P), IsOpen U → IsOpen O → R.Represents T → DifferentiableOn ℝ f O → (∀ y ∈ T.support ∩ O, f y = y) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict (R.carrier ∩ O)), f x = x ∧ ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, R.orient x (α.compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) = R.orient x α
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 7(a)–(c) of the parent proof ("π fixes S_i near B_G"). It is stated here for a general integer multiplicity current T, open set O and map f in place of S_i⌞B_G, B_{2G} and π_i. The good set M' := M ∩ O ∩ spt T replaces M_i ∩ B_G ∩ A_i; the parent applies the result with spt S_i ⊆ A_i.

Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n]. For x ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0, η_{x,r}(y) := r⁻¹(y − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap). HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n E x Q means finrank Q = n and ∫_{η_{x,r}(E)} φ dHⁿ → ∫_Q φ dHⁿ as r ↓ 0, for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) (Simon Ch. 3, 1.4).

1. (Hⁿ(M ∖ spt T) = 0.) spt T = U ∖ Z_T with Z_T open (SimonGMT isOpen_zeroRegion), so V := U ∖ spt T = U ∩ Z_T is open and V ⊆ U.
 (a) Every form ω admissible for M_V(T) has tsupport ω ⊆ V, which is disjoint from spt T, so T(ω) = 0 by the sibling vanish_off_support. Hence M_V(T) = 0.
 (b) By the sibling mass_eq_measure, μ_R(V) = M_V(T) = 0, where μ_R = θHⁿ⌞M.
 (c) Since θ ≥ 1 on M (field mult_pos), Hⁿ(M ∩ V) ≤ μ_R(V) = 0. As M ⊆ U, M ∖ spt T = M ∩ V.

2. (The good set.) Put M' := M ∩ O ∩ spt T. It is Borel, since spt T = U ∩ (ℝ^P ∖ Z_T). Moreover M' ⊆ M ∩ O and Hⁿ((M ∩ O) ∖ M') ≤ Hⁿ(M ∖ spt T) = 0 by step 1.

3. (Locality of approximate tangent spaces; parent 7(a).) Let x ∈ O and Q be a subspace with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q. Then HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q.
 (a) Let φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with spt φ ⊆ B_ρ(0), and d := dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ O) > 0 (d := ∞ if O = ℝ^P). For 0 < r < d/ρ, η_{x,r}(y) ∈ B_ρ(0) implies |y − x| < rρ < d, i.e. y ∈ O. So φ = 0 on η_{x,r}(M ∖ O), and since η_{x,r} is injective, ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} φ dHⁿ = ∫_{η_{x,r}(M∩O)} φ dHⁿ.
 (b) η_{x,r}(M ∩ O) is the disjoint union of η_{x,r}(M') and η_{x,r}((M ∩ O) ∖ M'). Since η_{x,r} is a similarity with ratio r⁻¹, Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(E)) = r^{−n}Hⁿ(E) for every E, so the second set is Hⁿ-null by step 2.
 (c) Therefore ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} φ dHⁿ = ∫_{η_{x,r}(M')} φ dHⁿ for all r ∈ (0, d/ρ), and both families have the same limit ∫_Q φ dHⁿ.

4. (Good points.)
 (a) By the field orients of R, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M there is a subspace Q_x with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q_x and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) Q_x. That is, there are an orthonormal basis τ₁, …, τₙ of Q_x and a sign s ∈ {1, −1} with ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ = s·α(τ₁, …, τₙ) for all α.

 (a) Suppose not. Then there are ε', r' > 0 such that |(z − x)/|z − x| − v| ≥ ε' for all z ∈ M' with 0 < |z − x| < r'.

subproblem.title: Push-forward of compactly supported integer multiplicity currents by a map that is C¹ near the support (Simon 6.2.23–2.29, 3.3–3.9)
subproblem.statement:
Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, O ⊆ ℝ^P open, and f : ℝ^P → ℝ^P C¹ on O (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O). Then there is a map push : 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) → 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with the following properties.
(A) Let Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) be integer multiplicity with spt Y compact and spt Y ⊆ O, and let (M, θ, ξ) be any integer multiplicity representation of Y. Then:
 (i) push Y(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·⟨ω(f(x)) ∘ ΛⁿDf(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P). Here (ω(f(x)) ∘ ΛⁿDf(x))(v₁, …, vₙ) = ω(f(x))(Df(x)v₁, …, Df(x)vₙ); in Lean, (ω (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x).
 (ii) push Y is integer multiplicity.
 (iii) spt push Y ⊆ f(spt Y).
 (iv) For every real L with ‖Df(y)‖ ≤ L for all y ∈ O, M(push Y) ≤ Lⁿ·M(Y), as ENNReal.ofReal (L^n) * M(Y).
 (v) If ∂Y = 0, then ∂(push Y) = 0.
(B) push(Y₁ − Y₂) = push Y₁ − push Y₂ for all integer multiplicity Y₁, Y₂ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with compact supports contained in O.
This is f_#Y of Simon 2.24(2) and 3.9.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (O : Set (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → Euclid P), IsOpen O → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O → ∃ push : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1) → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1), (∀ (Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)), R.Represents Y → IsCompact Y.support → Y.support ⊆ O → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1), push Y ω = ∫ x in R.carrier, (R.mult x : ℝ) * R.orient x (((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1)) (f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) ∂μHE[m + 1]) ∧ IsIntegerMultiplicity (push Y) ∧ (push Y).support ⊆ f '' Y.support ∧ (∀ L : ℝ, (∀ y ∈ O, ‖fderiv ℝ f y‖ ≤ L) → (push Y).mass ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (L ^ (m + 1)) * Y.mass) ∧ (Y.boundary = 0 → (push Y).boundary = 0)) ∧ ∀ Y₁ Y₂ : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1), IsIntegerMultiplicity Y₁ → IsIntegerMultiplicity Y₂ → IsCompact Y₁.support → Y₁.support ⊆ O → IsCompact Y₂.support → Y₂.support ⊆ O → push (Y₁ - Y₂) = push Y₁ - push Y₂
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, chapter-06.txt lines 404–530 and 770–860, with the area formula of Ch. 3, 2.4–2.6:
 • 2.23–2.24: push-forward and its boundary, and the explicit formula 2.24(2) for currents with locally finite mass and C¹ maps;
 • 2.27–2.29: homotopy estimate and mollified maps;
 • 3.3–3.9: push-forward of integer multiplicity currents by locally Lipschitz maps that are proper on the support; by 3.9, f_#T is integer multiplicity.
This is the result cited as (C3) in step 6 of the parent proof, with the properties listed there. The printed arguments are copied and specialised to a map f that is C¹ on an open set O containing the compact support. Two facts the source uses tacitly are proved in steps 2–3: additivity (B), and independence of the formula from the representation.

Notation. n = m + 1 and Hⁿ = μHE[n]. For an n-covector α and a linear map A, α ∘ ΛⁿA is the covector (v₁, …, vₙ) ↦ α(Av₁, …, Avₙ). For x ∈ O write Df(x) := fderiv ℝ f x. 𝒴 is the class of integer multiplicity Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with spt Y compact and contained in O. |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm.

1. (Preliminaries.)
 (a) Let v₁, …, vₙ ∈ ℝ^P and let V be the P×n matrix with columns vᵢ. By multilinearity and the alternating property, α(v₁, …, vₙ) = Σ_I α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)})·det(V_I), the sum over strictly increasing I : {1, …, n} → {1, …, P}, where V_I is the n×n submatrix of rows I. By Cauchy–Schwarz, |α(v₁, …, vₙ)| ≤ |α|·(Σ_I det(V_I)²)^{1/2}. By the Cauchy–Binet formula Σ_I det(V_I)² = det(VᵀV), the Gram determinant, which is at most Π_i|vᵢ|² by Hadamard's inequality. Now let τ₁, …, τₙ be orthonormal, ζ = ±τ₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ τₙ, and vᵢ := Aτᵢ. Then |⟨α ∘ ΛⁿA, ζ⟩| = |α(Aτ₁, …, Aτₙ)| ≤ |α|·Π_i|Aτᵢ| ≤ |α|·‖A‖ⁿ. For n = 0 both sides equal |α|.
 (b) Let Y ∈ 𝒴, K := spt Y, and (M, θ, ξ) a representation of Y. Then Hⁿ(M ∖ K) = 0. Indeed ℝ^P ∖ K is open and Y vanishes on forms supported there (vanish_off_support), so μ_Y(ℝ^P ∖ K) = M_{ℝ^P∖K}(Y) = 0 (mass_eq_measure), and θ ≥ 1 on M.
 (c) Df is continuous on O ⊇ K, so Λ_K := sup_K ‖Df‖ < ∞. Also μ_Y(K) < ∞ by local finiteness of the weight.

2. (Definition and independence of the representation; Simon 2.24(2), 3.3.)
 (a) For Y ∈ 𝒴 with a representation (M, θ, ξ) and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), let I(ω) := ∫_M θ⟨ω(f(x)) ∘ ΛⁿDf(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x).
 (b) By 1(a)–(c) the integrand is bounded by θ·sup|ω|·Λ_Kⁿ·1_K Hⁿ-a.e. on M. So the integral exists, is linear in ω, and |I(ω)| ≤ sup|ω|·Λ_Kⁿ·μ_Y(K). Hence I is sequentially continuous on test forms (TestFormOnConverges gives uniform convergence) and defines a current.
 (c) I does not depend on the representation. Choose χ ∈ C_c^∞(O) with χ = 1 on a neighbourhood of K, and put β(x) := χ(x)·(ω(f(x)) ∘ ΛⁿDf(x)), a continuous compactly supported n-form. By 1(b), I(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨β, ξ⟩ dHⁿ. Mollifying β gives smooth β_k with supports in a fixed compact set and β_k → β uniformly. By dominated convergence ∫_M θ⟨β, ξ⟩ dHⁿ = lim_k ∫_M θ⟨β_k, ξ⟩ dHⁿ = lim_k Y(β_k), which depends only on Y.
 (d) Define push Y := I for Y ∈ 𝒴, and push Y := 0 for Y ∉ 𝒴. Then (i) holds for every representation.

3. ((B) additivity.) Let Y₁, Y₂ ∈ 𝒴 with supports K₁, K₂.
 (a) Y₁ − Y₂ is integer multiplicity (im_calculus (c)). It vanishes on every form whose support misses the compact set K₁ ∪ K₂ ⊆ O (vanish_off_support for Y₁ and Y₂). So spt(Y₁ − Y₂) is compact and contained in K₁ ∪ K₂ (support_of_vanishing), and Y₁ − Y₂ ∈ 𝒴.
 (b) Take χ = 1 near K₁ ∪ K₂ in step 2. Then push(Y₁ − Y₂)(ω) = lim_k (Y₁ − Y₂)(β_k) = lim_k Y₁(β_k) − lim_k Y₂(β_k) = push Y₁(ω) − push Y₂(ω).

4. ((iii) support; Simon 2.29.) Let Y ∈ 𝒴. f(K) is compact, since f is continuous on O ⊇ K. If tsupport ω ∩ f(K) = ∅, then ω(f(x)) = 0 for x ∈ K, so by 1(b) the integrand in (i) vanishes Hⁿ-a.e. on M and push Y(ω) = 0. By support_of_vanishing (with U = ℝ^P and the compact set f(K)), spt push Y ⊆ f(K) = f(spt Y).

5. ((iv) mass; Simon 2.29.) Let L satisfy ‖Df(y)‖ ≤ L for y ∈ O. If O ≠ ∅ then L ≥ 0; if O = ∅ then K = ∅, μ_Y = 0 and push Y = 0. For every admissible ω (|ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y), by 1(a)(b): push Y(ω) ≤ ∫_M θ|ω(f(x))|·‖Df(x)‖ⁿ dHⁿ ≤ Lⁿ∫_M θ dHⁿ = Lⁿ·μ_Y(ℝ^P) = Lⁿ·M(Y), by mass_eq_measure with W = ℝ^P. Taking the supremum, M(push Y) ≤ Lⁿ·M(Y).

6. ((ii) integer multiplicity; Simon 3.5–3.9.) Let Y ∈ 𝒴 with representation (M, θ, ξ). By 1(b) we may replace M by M ∩ K.
 (a) Choose an open V with K ⊆ V and closure(V) ⊆ O compact. Near each point of closure(V), f is C¹ and Lipschitz.
 (b) On M the tangential differential d^M f_x : T_xM → ℝ^P exists Hⁿ-a.e., and d^M f_{x#}ξ(x) = Df(x)_#ξ(x), Df(x) restricted to T_xM (Simon Ch. 3, 2.2). So (i) reads push Y(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω(f(x)), d^M f_{x#}ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ.
 (c) Let M₊ := {x ∈ M : J^M f(x) > 0}. Points with J^M f = 0 contribute nothing, since there d^M f_{x#}ξ(x) = 0 (3.4). Since |d^M f_{x#}ξ(x)| = J^M f(x), the area formula (Ch. 3, 2.5) gives (3.6):
 push Y(ω) = ∫_{f(M₊)} ⟨ω(y), Σ_{x ∈ f⁻¹(y)∩M₊} θ(x) d^M f_{x#}ξ(x)/|d^M f_{x#}ξ(x)|⟩ dHⁿ(y).
 (d) f(M₊) is countably n-rectifiable, as a union of Lipschitz images of the pieces of M on which f is Lipschitz. So for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ f(M₊) the approximate tangent space T_y f(M₊) exists. For Hⁿ-a.e. such y the set f⁻¹(y) ∩ M₊ is finite (2.4), and each vector d^M f_{x#}ξ(x)/|d^M f_{x#}ξ(x)| with x in it equals ±η(y), for a unit simple n-vector η(y) orienting T_y f(M₊) (3.7).
 (e) Hence (3.8) Σ_x θ(x) d^M f_{x#}ξ(x)/|…| = N(y)η(y) with N(y) ∈ ℤ. Replacing η by −η where N < 0, push Y = τ(f(M₊) ∩ {N ≠ 0}, |N|, η) (3.9).
 (f) The multiplicity is locally integrable: ∫_{f(M₊)} |N| dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{f(M₊)} Σ_x θ(x) dHⁿ(y) = ∫_M θ J^M f dHⁿ ≤ Λ_Kⁿ·μ_Y(K) < ∞ (area formula 2.5).
 (g) Choosing Borel versions of the carrier, N and η, this is an integer multiplicity triple in ℝ^P representing push Y. So push Y is integer multiplicity.

7. ((v) boundary; Simon 2.24(1), 2.29.) Let Y ∈ 𝒴 with ∂Y = 0, and V as in step 6.
 (a) Let χ₁ ∈ C_c^∞(O) with χ₁ = 1 on a neighbourhood of closure(V), and f_σ := (χ₁f) ∗ φ_σ for σ > 0 (mollification). Then f_σ is smooth on ℝ^P, and f_σ → f, Df_σ → Df uniformly on closure(V) as σ ↓ 0, because f is C¹ near closure(V).
 (b) For the smooth map g := f_σ, Simon 2.23 defines g_#Y(ω) := Y(ζ g^#ω) with ζ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^P), ζ = 1 near K; the value does not depend on ζ.
 (c) By 2.24(1), ∂g_#Y = g_#∂Y = 0. Indeed ∂g_#Y(ω) = Y(ζ g^#dω) = Y(ζ d(g^#ω)) = Y(d(ζ g^#ω)) − Y(dζ ∧ g^#ω) = (∂Y)(ζ g^#ω) − 0 = 0, because dζ ∧ g^#ω vanishes near K = spt Y.
 (d) By 2.24(2), g_#Y(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω(f_σ(x)) ∘ ΛⁿDf_σ(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ. As σ ↓ 0 this tends to push Y(ω), by dominated convergence (uniform convergence on K and the bound of step 2).
 (e) Hence ∂(push Y)(ω) = push Y(dω) = lim_σ f_{σ#}Y(dω) = lim_σ ∂(f_{σ#}Y)(ω) = 0 for every ω. ∎
proof_key_steps: For Y with compact support K ⊆ O, push Y(ω) := ∫_M θ⟨ω(f(x)) ∘ ΛⁿDf(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ (2.24(2)) is a current. It does not depend on the representation (approximate the continuous form χ·f^#ω by smooth forms), and push Y := 0 otherwise.
Additivity follows from independence of the representation. The support lies in f(K), since the integrand vanishes off f⁻¹(spt ω).
Mass: |⟨α ∘ ΛⁿA, ξ⟩| ≤ |α|·‖A‖ⁿ (Cauchy–Binet, Hadamard) gives M(push Y) ≤ Lⁿ·M(Y).
Integer multiplicity by the area formula: push Y = τ(f(M₊), |N|, ±η) with N integer valued (3.6–3.9).
If ∂Y = 0 then ∂(push Y) = 0: push Y is the weak limit of push-forwards by smooth mollified maps, which commute with ∂ (2.24(1), 2.29).

subproblem.title: Slicing an integer multiplicity current with integer multiplicity boundary by a Lipschitz function (Simon 6.4.1–4.5, 4.8)
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ with m + 1 < P. Let T ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(ℝ^P) be represented by an integer multiplicity triple R_T = (M, θ, ξ) (IMRep univ (m + 2), R_T.Represents T), and let ∂T ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) be represented by an integer multiplicity triple R_∂ = (M', θ', ξ') (IMRep univ (m + 1)). Let f : ℝ^P → ℝ be Lipschitz with constant L ∈ [0, ∞) (LipschitzWith L f). subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 4.1, Remark 4.2, 4.3, Definition 4.4, Lemma 4.5 and 4.8 (chapter-06.txt lines 1151–1360, printed pp. 153–158). They are applied to the integer multiplicity (m+2)-current T = τ(M, θ, ξ) in U = ℝ^P; Simon's n is m + 2 here and the slices are (m+1)-currents. This is the result cited as (C2) in step 5 of the parent proof. The printed proofs are copied. Two points the source leaves implicit are made explicit: the family P_t is defined for every t, by the right side of 4.5(2) (step 1), and t ↦ M_W(P_t) is measurable (step 6). The hypothesis m + 1 < P only ensures that the currents considered are not trivially zero; it is not otherwise used.

Notation.
 • N := m + 2 and Hᵏ := μHE[k].
 • For x ∈ M, ∇^M f(x) is the gradient of f along M (Simon Ch. 3, 2.1). It is defined Hᴺ-a.e. on M through a decomposition M = ⋃_j M_j with Hᴺ(M₀) = 0 and M_j ⊆ N_j, N_j embedded C¹ submanifolds, and |∇^M f| ≤ L Hᴺ-a.e. on M.
 • M₊ := {x ∈ M : ∇^M f(x) ≠ 0}, and M_t := M₊ ∩ f⁻¹(t) for t ∈ ℝ.
 Borel versions of ∇^M f and of M₊ are fixed; this changes nothing up to Hᴺ-null sets.

1. (The currents P_t.) For every t, E_t := {f < t} is open, since f is continuous.
 (a) By the sibling im_calculus (b) (restriction of a representation to a Borel set, U = ℝ^P) there are currents A_t ∈ 𝒟_N(ℝ^P) and B_t ∈ 𝒟_{N−1}(ℝ^P) represented by (M ∩ E_t, θ, ξ) and (M' ∩ E_t, θ', ξ'). These are Simon's T⌞{f < t} and (∂T)⌞{f < t}.
 (b) Put P_t := ∂A_t − B_t. For every ω ∈ 𝒟^{N−1}(ℝ^P), P_t(ω) = A_t(dω) − B_t(ω) = ∫_{M∩{f<t}} θ⟨dω, ξ⟩ dHᴺ − ∫_{M'∩{f<t}} θ'⟨ω, ξ'⟩ dH^{N−1}. This is the identity in (2), and it holds for every t.

2. (Lemma 4.1: coarea on M.) For L¹-a.e. t the following hold.
 (a) M_t is countably (N−1)-rectifiable (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 2.10(2)).
 (b) For H^{N−1}-a.e. x ∈ M_t, the approximate tangent spaces T_xM_t and T_xM exist, T_xM_t is an (N−1)-dimensional subspace of T_xM, and T_xM = {y + λ∇^M f(x) : y ∈ T_xM_t, λ ∈ ℝ}. This follows from Simon Ch. 3, 1.6 applied to M_t and to M, together with ∇^M f(x) ∈ T_xM and ⟨∇^M f(x), τ⟩ = 0 for τ ∈ T_xM_t (Ch. 3, 2.1).
 (c) For every non-negative Hᴺ-measurable g on M, ∫_ℝ ∫_{M_t} g dH^{N−1} dt = ∫_M |∇^M f| g dHᴺ, and t ↦ ∫_{M_t} g dH^{N−1} is L¹-measurable. This is the co-area formula, Simon Ch. 3, 2.8–2.9 with m = 1.
 Replacing g by g·1_{f<t} gives Remark 4.2: t ↦ ∫_{M∩{f<t}} |∇^M f| g dHᴺ = ∫_{−∞}^t ∫_{M_s} g dH^{N−1} ds is absolutely continuous, with derivative ∫_{M_t} g dH^{N−1} for a.e. t.

3. (4.3–4.4: the slice as an integer multiplicity current.) Take t as in step 2.
 (a) For H^{N−1}-a.e. x ∈ M_t, ξ_t(x) := ξ(x) ⌞ (∇^M f(x)/|∇^M f(x)|) (with ⟨ξ⌞w, a⟩ := ⟨ξ, w ∧ a⟩) is a unit simple (N−1)-vector orienting T_xM_t. Indeed (4.3), ξ(x) = ±τ₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ τ_N with τ₁ = ∇^M f/|∇^M f| and τ₂, …, τ_N an orthonormal basis of T_xM_t.
 (b) Let θ_t := θ|M_t. By step 2(c) with g = θ1_K, ∫_ℝ ∫_{M_t∩K} θ dH^{N−1} dt ≤ L∫_{M∩K} θ dHᴺ < ∞ for each compact K. Applying this to K = closedBall(0, k), k ∈ ℕ, θ_t is locally H^{N−1}-integrable on M_t for a.e. t.
 (c) Fix a Borel version ξ̃ of ξ; ξ is Hᴺ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable. Let Z ⊆ M be an Hᴺ-null Borel set containing the points where ξ̃ ≠ ξ, where ξ does not orient T_xM, or where ∇^M f or T_xM does not exist. By step 2(c) with g = 1_Z, ∫_ℝ H^{N−1}(Z ∩ M_t) dt = ∫_Z |∇^M f| dHᴺ = 0, so H^{N−1}(Z ∩ M_t) = 0 for a.e. t. Hence for a.e. t, (a) holds at H^{N−1}-a.e. x ∈ M_t, and ξ_t agrees H^{N−1}-a.e. on M_t with the Borel field ξ̃ ⌞ (∇^M f/|∇^M f|).
 (d) Hence for a.e. t, (M_t, θ_t, ξ_t) is an integer multiplicity triple (an IMRep univ (N−1)): Borel carrier, countably (N−1)-rectifiable, θ_t ≥ 1 integer valued and locally integrable, ξ_t measurable and orienting the approximate tangent spaces a.e.
 (e) ⟨T, f, t⟩ := τ(M_t, θ_t, ξ_t) ∈ 𝒟_{N−1}(ℝ^P) is then an integer multiplicity current: im_calculus (b) with E = ℝ^P provides the current, the functional being sequentially continuous by local integrability.

4. (4.5(2): ⟨T, f, t⟩ = P_t for a.e. t.)
 (a) Fix ω ∈ 𝒟^{N−1}(ℝ^P), t ∈ ℝ and ε > 0. Let γ_ε : ℝ → [0, 1] equal 1 on (−∞, t − ε], 0 on [t, ∞), and be linear on [t − ε, t]. Then h := γ_ε ∘ f is Lipschitz, and its mollification h^{(σ)} := h ∗ φ_σ (Simon Ch. 2, §2) is smooth.
 (b) (∂T)(h^{(σ)}ω) = T(d(h^{(σ)}ω)) = T(dh^{(σ)} ∧ ω) + T(h^{(σ)} dω).
 (c) Since ξ(x) orients T_xM, ⟨ξ(x), dh^{(σ)}(x) ∧ ω(x)⟩ = ⟨ξ(x) ⌞ ∇^M h^{(σ)}(x), ω(x)⟩. As σ ↓ 0, ∇^M h^{(σ)} → ∇^M h weakly in L²(μ_T) on M. This is Simon's (1), checked on each C¹ piece N_j using the uniform convergence of h^{(σ)} to h. Hence lim_{σ↓0} T(dh^{(σ)} ∧ ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ξ ⌞ ∇^M h, ω⟩ dHᴺ.
 (d) By the chain rule (Simon's (4)), ∇^M h = γ_ε'(f)∇^M f Hᴺ-a.e. on M, since ∇^M f = 0 a.e. on level sets of f. Also h^{(σ)}ω → hω and h^{(σ)}dω → h dω uniformly, with supports in a fixed compact set. Using the representations of T and ∂T, (b) and (c) give
 ∫_{M'} θ' h⟨ω, ξ'⟩ dH^{N−1} = −ε^{−1}∫_{M∩{t−ε<f<t}} θ⟨ξ ⌞ ∇^M f, ω⟩ dHᴺ + ∫_M θ h⟨dω, ξ⟩ dHᴺ.
 (e) Let ε ↓ 0. By dominated convergence (h → 1_{f<t}), the left side tends to B_t(ω) and the last term to A_t(dω). Apply Remark 4.2 (step 2) with g := θ⟨ξ ⌞ (∇^M f/|∇^M f|), ω⟩, split into positive and negative parts: the middle term tends to −∫_{M_t} θ⟨ξ_t, ω⟩ dH^{N−1} = −⟨T, f, t⟩(ω) for every t outside an L¹-null set F_ω. Hence ⟨T, f, t⟩(ω) = A_t(dω) − B_t(ω) = P_t(ω) for t ∉ F_ω.
 (f) Take a countable set Ω ⊆ 𝒟^{N−1}(ℝ^P) such that every ω is the limit of some ω_k ∈ Ω with supports in a fixed compact set and ω_k → ω, dω_k → dω uniformly (Simon: "by considering a countable dense set of ω"). Put F := ⋃_{ω ∈ Ω} F_ω, an L¹-null set. Both sides are continuous in ω for this convergence: |P_t(ω)| ≤ sup|dω| μ_T(K) + sup|ω| μ_{∂T}(K), and |⟨T, f, t⟩(ω)| ≤ sup|ω| ∫_{M_t∩K} θ dH^{N−1} < ∞ for a.e. t. So ⟨T, f, t⟩ = P_t for a.e. t.

5. (4.8: support.) For t as in steps 2–4, ⟨T, f, t⟩ = τ(M_t, θ_t, ξ_t) with M_t ⊆ f⁻¹(t). If tsupport ω ∩ f⁻¹(t) = ∅, then ω = 0 on M_t, so P_t(ω) = ⟨T, f, t⟩(ω) = 0. Together with step 3, P_t is integer multiplicity and vanishes on such ω for a.e. t; with the identity of step 1, which holds for every t, this proves (2).

6. (4.5(1) and measurability.) Let W be open.
 (a) For a.e. t, P_t = ⟨T, f, t⟩ is integer multiplicity with representation (M_t, θ_t, ξ_t). By the sibling mass_eq_measure (with U = ℝ^P), M_W(P_t) = ∫_{M_t∩W} θ dH^{N−1}.
 (b) By step 2(c) with g = θ1_W, the right side is an L¹-measurable function of t. So t ↦ M_W(P_t) is a.e.-measurable.
 (c) Using |∇^M f| ≤ L Hᴺ-a.e. (f is L-Lipschitz) and mass_eq_measure for T: ∫_ℝ M_W(P_t) dt = ∫_ℝ ∫_{M_t∩W} θ dH^{N−1} dt = ∫_{M∩W} |∇^M f| θ dHᴺ ≤ L ∫_{M∩W} θ dHᴺ = L·μ_T(W) = L·M_W(T). This proves (1). ∎
proof_key_steps: Define P_t := ∂A_t − B_t for every t, with A_t, B_t the restrictions of T and ∂T to {f < t} (im_calculus (b)). This is the stated integral formula.
Coarea on M (Lemma 4.1): for a.e. t, M_t = M₊ ∩ f⁻¹(t) is countably (m+1)-rectifiable with T_xM = T_xM_t ⊕ ℝ∇^M f, and ∫_ℝ ∫_{M_t} g = ∫_M |∇^M f| g.
For a.e. t, ⟨T, f, t⟩ = τ(M_t, θ, ξ⌞∇^M f/|∇^M f|) is integer multiplicity (4.3–4.4).
Mollification and Remark 4.2 give ⟨T, f, t⟩ = P_t for a.e. t (4.5(2)); a countable dense family of forms makes the null set independent of ω.
P_t is carried by f⁻¹(t) (4.8). M_W(P_t) = ∫_{M_t∩W} θ is measurable in t, with integral ∫_{M∩W} |∇^M f| θ ≤ L·M_W(T) (4.5(1), mass_eq_measure).

subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, A ⊆ ℝ^P, and S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) minimizing in A (IsMinimizingIn S A) with spt S ⊆ A. Let G > 0 with closedBall(0, G) ⊆ U, and L ≥ 0. Let π : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be C¹ on B_{2G}(0), with π(B_{2G}(0)) ⊆ A, π(y) = y for y ∈ A ∩ B_{2G}(0), and |π(y)| ≤ 2|y| and |π(y) − π(z)| ≤ L|y − z| for y, z ∈ B_{2G}(0). Let Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) be integer multiplicity with ∂Y = 0, spt Y compact and spt Y ⊆ B_{G/2}(0). Then M_{B_G(0)}(S) ≤ Lⁿ·M_{B_G(0)}(S + Y). Here S + Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U) means S − (0 − Y|_U), with Y|_U := Y.restrictDomain (U ⊆ ℝ^P), and Lⁿ is read as ENNReal.ofReal (L^n).

Source: steps 6 and 7 of the parent proof, stated for one index: the competitor Z_i = S_i + π_{i#}Y_i, minimality of S_i in A_i, π_{i#}Q_i = Q_i and the estimate (I). The parent applies it with S = S_i, A = A_i, U = U_i, π = π_i, L = 1 + η and Y = Y_i, where spt Y_i ⊆ B_{G/3}(0).

Siblings used: pushforward (PF), orientation_fixed (OF), measure_subadditive (F4), mass_eq_measure (M), vanish_off_support (V), im_calculus (b) restriction and (c) differences, restrict_domain_im (RD), support_of_vanishing (SV).

Notation. n := m + 1 and B_r := ball(0, r). ι is the inclusion of 𝒟ⁿ(U) into 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (same form). For currents A, B in one domain, A + B := A − (0 − B), so (A + B)(ω) = A(ω) + B(ω). The zero current is integer multiplicity, since it equals A − A for any integer multiplicity A (im_calculus (c)).

1. (Derivative bound.) π is C¹ and L-Lipschitz on the open ball B_{2G}, with L ≥ 0. So ‖Dπ(y)‖ ≤ L for y ∈ B_{2G} (Mathlib norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitzOn).

2. (Q := S⌞B_G as a current in ℝ^P.) Let (M, θ, ξ) represent S; S is integer multiplicity by the first part of IsMinimizingIn.
 (a) By im_calculus (b) (with U and E = B_G), (M ∩ B_G, θ, ξ) is an integer multiplicity triple in U. Since M ∩ B_G ⊆ closedBall(0, G), a compact subset of U, its multiplicity is integrable over every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P: ∫_{M∩B_G∩K} θ ≤ ∫_{M∩closedBall(0,G)} θ < ∞.
 (b) So the same data form an integer multiplicity triple in ℝ^P. By im_calculus (b) (with ℝ^P and E = ℝ^P) it represents a current Q ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), with carrier M ∩ B_G and weight μ_Q = μ_S⌞B_G.
 (Q1) If ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and tsupport ω ⊆ B_G, then S(ω) = Q(ιω). Both are ∫θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ, over M and over M ∩ B_G respectively, and ω = 0 on M ∖ B_G.
 (Q2) spt Q ⊆ K_Q := closedBall(0, G) ∩ spt S. This set is compact (it equals closedBall(0, G) ∖ Z_S, as closedBall(0, G) ⊆ U) and contained in A ∩ B_{2G} (as spt S ⊆ A). Indeed Hⁿ(M ∖ spt S) = 0, because μ_S(U ∖ spt S) = 0 by V and M and θ ≥ 1. If tsupport ω ∩ K_Q = ∅, then ω(x) = 0 for every x ∈ (M ∩ B_G) ∩ spt S. So the integrand of Q(ω) vanishes Hⁿ-a.e. on M ∩ B_G, and Q(ω) = 0. SV gives spt Q ⊆ K_Q, and spt Q is compact.

3. (Push-forward.) Apply PF with O := B_{2G} and f := π, which is C¹ on O. This gives push with properties (i)–(v) and (B). Q and Y are in its domain: both are integer multiplicity with compact supports contained in B_{2G}, since spt Q ⊆ closedBall(0, G) and spt Y ⊆ B_{G/2}.
 (Q3) push Q = Q.
 (a) Apply OF to Q with its representation (M ∩ B_G, θ, ξ), U := ℝ^P, O := B_{2G} and f := π, which is differentiable on O. Its hypothesis holds: for y ∈ spt Q ∩ B_{2G} we have y ∈ spt S ⊆ A, so π(y) = y.
 (b) Hence for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ B_G (⊆ B_{2G}): π(x) = x and ⟨α ∘ ΛⁿDπ(x), ξ(x)⟩ = ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ for all α.
 (c) By PF (i), push Q(ω) = ∫_{M∩B_G} θ⟨ω(π(x)) ∘ ΛⁿDπ(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ = ∫_{M∩B_G} θ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ = Q(ω).

4. (Additivity.) 0 − Y is integer multiplicity with spt(0 − Y) = spt Y, since (0 − Y)(ω) = −Y(ω) and so the zero regions coincide; and spt 0 = ∅.
 (a) PF (B) with (0, 0) gives push 0 = push 0 − push 0, hence push 0 = 0.
 (b) PF (B) with (0, Y) gives push(0 − Y) = 0 − push Y.

 (b) Q + Y is integer multiplicity, with compact support in K_Q ∪ spt Y ⊆ B_{2G}: it vanishes on forms supported off this compact set, and SV applies. By PF (iv) and step 1, M(push(Q + Y)) ≤ Lⁿ·M(Q + Y).
 (c) M(Q + Y) = M_{B_G}(Q + Y). By F4 (with c = 1), μ_{Q+Y} ≤ μ_Q + μ_Y. Also μ_Q(ℝ^P ∖ B_G) = 0, since its carrier M ∩ B_G lies in B_G, and μ_Y(ℝ^P ∖ B_G) ≤ μ_Y(ℝ^P ∖ spt Y) = 0 by V and M. So μ_{Q+Y}(ℝ^P ∖ B_G) = 0, and by M, M(Q + Y) = μ_{Q+Y}(ℝ^P) = μ_{Q+Y}(B_G) = M_{B_G}(Q + Y).
 (d) M_{B_G}(Q + Y) ≤ M_{B_G}(S + Y|_U). Every ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) admissible for M_{B_G} lies in 𝒟ⁿ(U), as tsupport ω' ⊆ B_G ⊆ U, and (Q + Y)(ω') = S(ω') + Y(ω') = (S + Y|_U)(ω') by (Q1).
